title: VTC Admin Events — shared definitions
description:
Shared shapes for a Verifiable Trust Community's live administrative console events: a hint-only channel that tells an administrator's console WHEN to re-read, never WHAT changed.

THE MODEL. A console subscribes once per session with `vtc/admin/events/subscribe`, naming the topics it renders. The community answers with a stream of `vtc/admin/events/event` documents, each naming one topic and, for a count topic, the caller's current count. An event carries no record and no personal data. The console reacts by re-fetching the topic's own signed read, so the read stays the only place authorization is decided and the only place data leaves the community: the stream can neither leak a record nor grant a read. Polling those reads remains the fallback whenever the stream is down.

TOPICS AND THEIR READS. Each topic names one read. A community sends a topic's events only to a caller it would answer on that read.

- `actions` — the caller's visible administrative actions (`vtc/admin/actions/list`). Count topic: the caller's `waitingForMe` count.
- `acknowledgements` — the acknowledge-category actions awaiting the caller (`vtc/admin/actions/list`). Count topic: the open acknowledge actions the caller has not yet acknowledged.
- `joinRequests` — the community's join requests (`vtc/join-requests/list`). Count topic: the join requests awaiting a decision.
- `members` — the community's members (`vtc/members/list`). No count.
- `singleAdminMode` — whether single-administrator mode is in effect. Every administrator may read it. No count.
- `config` — the community's stored configuration (`vtc/config/export`). No count.

Topic.title: Topic
Topic.description: One kind of change a console can be told about. A closed set: a topic not listed here is a new MINOR version of this component, not an `ext` member, because each topic is bound to the read that authorizes it.

ResumeToken.title: ResumeToken
ResumeToken.description: Opaque, community-minted position in one caller's event stream. A console MUST NOT parse, construct or order it; it only hands the latest one back as `since` when it re-subscribes. A community binds it to the caller it was minted for and treats a token minted for anyone else as unknown.
